Título: Symbiotic Artificial Intelligence Twin Framework for Circular Manufacturing: A Sustainability-Led Industry 5.0 Framework
Autores: P, Rathnavel
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE 7th International Conference on Computing, Communication and Automation (ICCCA)
Abstract: Industry 5.0 or the fifth industrial revolution is a natural transition from industrial paradigms that are automation-centric towards symbiotic human-machine systems, which focus on sustainability, social purpose, and resilience within industrial ecosystems. In this paper, a Symbiotic AI-Twin Framework (SATF) is proposed for circular manufacturing systems to align intelligent automation with sustainability. SATF combines one or more cognitive digital twins for the real-time mirroring of systems with edge artificial intelligence (AI) employing federated learning for distributed decision-making, while involving a human-in-the-loop (HITL) to provide interactivity and adaptability to human stakeholders. Essentially, SATF demonstrates that the use of bio-inspired optimization methods in combination with supply chain mapping will help prevent the loss of materials and waste, while the scheduling methods informed by external sources with carbon-awareness will ensure that operational practices are sustainable given associated environmental limits and renewable energy sources. SATF was simulated as virtual factory environments with significant sustainability outcomes, including measurable sustainability reports containing, on one instance, a 65% increase in material reuse contributions to the bottom line to values upwards of 91% energy efficiency, to examples of reducing products carbon footprint sourcing from 0.52 kg CO₂e units to .23 kg per product unit. These findings represent SATFs modelling and conceptual function given the parallels of other next generation green manufacturing systems and the legacy associated with industry 5.0 framework with a circular economy lens.

Título: Exploring AI-Driven Supply Chain Innovations from Industry 4.0 to 6.0: A Comprehensive Review
Autores: Verma, Deepti and Singhal, Ritesh and Pandita, Sarjue and Garg, Ankit and Singh, Akash and M, Anirudh N
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE 7th International Conference on Computing, Communication and Automation (ICCCA)
Abstract: The following study looks at how supply chains are changing because of artificial intelligence (AI) as businesses across the globe shift from Industry 4.0 to Industry 6.0. It emphasizes the ways in which AI improves greater human-machine collaboration, increases productivity, and facilitates environmentally friendly behavior. The study utilized research from 2010 to 2023 drawn from peer-reviewed databases such as Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect with systematic review methodology (PRISMA). Atlas.ti software was employed by the authors in order to identify noteworthy trends in employing AI within supply chain management after choosing the most pertinent papers. The study provides insights into how AI is significantly contributing to vital functions like inventory management, demand planning, and data-driven, timely decision-making. Supply chains are becoming more responsive and tailored because Industry 5.0 is increasingly focusing on human-AI collaboration. AI also contributes to the environment by assisting companies in utilizing AI resources more efficiently and minimizing waste. There are nonetheless issues, including safeguarding employees from such change and making systems cyber proof. Overall, the study offers good insight into how to best incorporate AI into smart, sustainable, and future-proof supply chains for researchers and practitioners.

Título: Multi-Objective Optimization and Cyber-Physical Integration for Sustainable Manufacturing in Industry 5.0
Autores: Dhatterwal, Jagjit Singh and Chahar, Suman and Malik, Kiran
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE 7th International Conference on Computing, Communication and Automation (ICCCA)
Abstract: Furthermore, the development of manufacturing from Industry 4.0 to Industry 5.0, requires paradigm changes towards sustainable, resilient and human-centered industrial ecosystems. In this paper, a methodology is proposed with the aim of designing a holistic framework for the integration between MOO and CPS to render sustainable manufacturing in a way that is congruent with Industry 5.0 principles. Using a system-theories point of view and data-driven intelligence, we will cope with trade-offs of contradicting objectives (productivity, energy efficiency, environmental impact, or well-being of workers) in the dynamic factory context. Our approach is based on real-time sensor data, digital twins and machine learning for decision support throughout the product lifecycle. We introduce an optimization framework which integrates Pareto-based evolutionary algorithms and reinforcement learning for adaptive control in complex CPS. In addition, we introduce human-in-the-loop-design to guarantee transparency, to empower workers, and to improve system resilience in the face of uncertainty. Taking case studies in smart manufacturing, our framework realizes remarkable energy efficient (up to 27%), carbon footprint decreased (by 18%), and worker satisfaction score improvement, verifying its practicality in human-cyber-physical coordination. We also discuss policy implications and ethical issues related to responsible technology implementation. This work adds to growing debate on Industry 5.0 by bridging computational techniques with social technical viewpoints. It offers a flexible, integrated model for future-fit manufacturing systems which are based on commitment to sustainability, resilience and human well-being. The approach provides theoretical understanding as well as practical instruments for engineers, researchers and policy makers to create a balanced, post-industrial manufacturing system.

Título: Integrating ISO 50001:2018 into Engineering Education: Advancing Energy skills for Industry 4.0 and 5.0
Autores: Ali, Marwa Ben and Rauch, Erwin
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 11th International Conference on Control, Decision and Information Technologies (CoDIT)
Abstract: The present paper explores the integration of ISO 50001 energy management standards into engineering education in Europe, aiming to align academic training with the demands of Industry 4.0 (I4.0) and Industry 5.0 (I5.0), as well as the evolving technologies and regulations. It underscores the strategic importance of equipping future engineers with the competencies necessary for energy efficiency, sustainability reporting, and smart sustainable industrial practices. By embedding ISO 50001 into curricula, students can acquire essential skills that enhance their employability, innovation potential, and readiness to contribute to modern energy management systems. The paper also discusses the mutual benefits for companies, including smoother implementation of energy strategies and a workforce better prepared for sustainability-driven transformation. Despite its potential, ISO 50001 adoption remains limited, with many companies still hesitant, highlighting the need for stronger educational-industry collaboration and curriculum reform. However, this approach of academia-industry collaboration could serve as a starting point for initiating the internal audit towards external certification.

Título: Harnessing Lean and Industry 4.0 for Sustainable and Zero-Waste Warehousing: A Conceptual Framework Toward Lean 5.0
Autores: Kihel, Yousra El and Bouyahrouzi, El Mahdi and Embarki, Soufiane and Sehli, Lotfi and Kihel, Bachir El
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE 13th International Conference on Intelligent Data Acquisition and Advanced Computing Systems: Technology and Applications (IDAACS)
Abstract: The fast expansion of Industry 4.0 technologies creates new opportunity to reinvent traditional warehousing practices, yet the difficulty of removing systematic waste persists. Although Lean Manufacturing has long been acknowledged as a key to waste reduction, its integration with I4.0 technologies remains unexplored in the context of smart warehouses. This article provides a dynamic conceptual framework that combines Industry 4.0 technology and Lean principles to create sustainable, zero-waste storage, paving the path for Lean 5.0. The proposed framework addresses both overt wastes-such as overproduction and excess inventory-and more subtle inefficiencies, such as energy losses and process variability, by incorporating real-time data analytics, RFID and barcode, and automated decisionmaking and storage into Lean methodologies such as Value Stream Mapping and Just-In-Time. A case study done at a Moroccan beverage bottling facility revealed a 30% decrease in inventory-related waste and a $25 \%$ increase in operational throughput achieved by IoT-enabled inventory monitoring and AI-driven demand forecasting, respectively. Furthermore, the application of Machine Learning algorithms strengthens Lean’s kaizen concept by allowing for proactive waste detection and detailed root cause investigation. This scalable, technology-agnostic paradigm combines the theoretical goals of Lean with the practical needs of Industry 4.0, laying the groundwork for a new age of Lean 5.0 centered on sustainability and zero waste.

Título: Technician Utilization-Based Analysis of Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) and Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) for a Strategic Approach in Failure Corrective Maintenance System (FCMS)
Autores: Vejjanugraha, Pikul and Pawasarn, Wuttipong
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 20th International Joint Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing (iSAI-NLP)
Abstract: In Industry 4.0 and 5.0 environments, reliability and efficiency are vital to maintaining competitiveness, as unplanned downtime can cause severe operational losses. This study presents a technician utilization–based analysis of Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) and Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) within a Failure Corrective Maintenance System (FCMS). Results show that high technician utilization extends MTTR due to workload saturation, whereas low utilization delays MTTD because of limited inspections. A Pareto analysis reveals that 20% of technicians account for over 80% of total maintenance activities, indicating a significant imbalance in workload distribution. To address this, a strategic framework is proposed emphasizing balanced technician allocation, skill-based task assignment, and digital monitoring integration. The proposed approach aims to optimize workforce utilization, enhance responsiveness, and improve system reliability. The contribution of this work lies in offering actionable guidelines by define technician utilization thresholds at 55-75% as the optimal threshold for balanced workload for industries seeking to strengthen workforce efficiency, minimize downtime, and sustain resilience in advanced industrial ecosystems.

Título: Human Centered Industry 5.0 Data Representation in the context of Technology Driven Digital Transformation Interfacing
Autores: Korodi, Adrian and Vesa, Vlad-Cristian and Dontu, Raul-Andrei
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE 23rd International Conference on Industrial Informatics (INDIN)
Abstract: Targeting efficiency increase means to approach digital transformation and to apply Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and Industry 4.0 concepts. The backbone of digital transformation is interfacing and connectivity. The ongoing battle with legacy protocols and solutions in the operational technology (OT) level is expanding with the necessity to cope and work with information technology (IT) level legacy systems that are presenting a completely different perspective. Industry 5.0 comes to consolidate previous advances with a societal vision, having a human centric apprehension as one of the main pillars. The current work is focusing on establishing a foundation for a single-source-of-truth human-oriented data representation in a context of a virtual unified space for digital transformation. The chosen transport protocol is Message Queue Telemetry Transport (MQTT) and data is transmitted in a structured and contextualized form using JSON and Sparkplug B. The physical objects from industrial processes contain graphic descriptors and defined templates that increase human perception, creative initiative and guiding capabilities, making him able to be in the center of decision making. The other two pillars of Industry 5.0, sustainability and resilience are also positively influenced by the improved representation and perception on all levels, including possibilities of decentralized decision making and AI guiding. The applicability of the solution can be both on the IT and OT levels, including the cloud, either in process control independent applications. The solution is tested successfully using Ignition environment set to function in the MQTT and Sparkplug configuration and an external software application that can be placed on any hierarchical level and set to interface using MQTT. The presented case-study considers an OT-IT integration with a SCADA node and an external Node-RED application that interfaces and integrates a complete user-defined data type template.

Título: Beyond Signature-based Defense: Deep Learning Frameworks for Concealed Cyber Exploit Detection
Autores: Hariharasudhan, S. and Rajeshwari, S. and Priyadharshini, S. V. and K, Vishnu Priya and Santhoshkumar, S. P. and S, Gajalakshmi
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 6th International Conference on IoT Based Control Networks and Intelligent Systems (ICICNIS)
Abstract: The emergence of intelligent manufacturing due to Industry 4.0 and 5.0 frameworks increased the exposure to dependence on deep learning systems, which are ideal targets of advanced cyber-attacks. Traditional cybersecurity techniques are becoming insufficient to deal with the emerging trends, including covert attacks like backdoor attacks that interfere with the model integrity during the training of the model and interfere with outputs. A new, multi-layered smart cyber defence framework demanding a combination of threat modelling, data protection, and model protection has been presented in this paper to protect deep learning concept. The framework model is a permutation of both statistical and intelligent methods to avoid data privacy and confidentiality and extends structural measures of security management in terms of policies and procedures. It also presents ways of improving the sturdiness of models alongside attacks with the help of an adaptive threat model to identify the vulnerable points and implement countermeasures efficiently. An overview of back door attacks and defence mechanisms to back door attacks is given and a qualitative comparison of strategies in existence has been made. Last but not least, the paper identifies the future research directions to enhance exploit detection in deep learning by providing detailed suggestions on how the research can be taken further to promote research in resilient cyber defence towards the smart manufacturing systems.

Título: Autonomous Systems in Industry 5.0 Revolutionizing Efficiency, Collaboration and Sustainability
Autores: Kok, Chiang Liang and Heng, Jovan Bowen and Lizheng, Nicholas Tan and Tang, Howard and Teo, Tee Hui
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Recent Advances in Systems Science and Engineering (RASSE)
Abstract: Autonomous systems are becoming the cornerstone of Industry 5.0, enabling industries to merge the precision and scalability of automation with human-centric and sustainable practices. These systems integrate advanced artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), robotics, and the Internet of Things (IoT) to optimize operations, enhance decision-making, and foster collaborative work environments. This paper delves into the transformative potential of autonomous systems in diverse sectors such as logistics, manufacturing, healthcare, and urban planning. It further addresses key challenges, including regulatory barriers, societal acceptance, and technical limitations, while proposing innovative solutions. Additionally, the interplay between semiautonomous systems and fully autonomous solutions is explored, offering insights into future applications and the ethical considerations required for responsible deployment. Relevant realworld case studies, emerging technologies, and available research references are included to provide a holistic understanding of the field.

Título: An Internet-of-Things platform for environmental monitoring of the workplace in winemaking industry: proof-of-concept for the Industry 5.0 framework
Autores: Sansone, Francesco and Sanmartin, Chiara and Venturi, Francesca and Tonacci, Alessandro
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE 25th International Symposium on Computational Intelligence and Informatics (CINTI)
Abstract: In the wine industry, one of the main challenges is represented by environmental sustainability, not only limited to the preservation of the surrounding environment but also relying on good practices to make the working environment safe and sustainable for the employees. In such a framework, Industry 5.0 comes into help, leveraging Information and Communication Technology to enable the design and development of safe, secure workplaces, minimizing risks for the employees for both accidents and fatalities, and long-term consequences of exposure to pollutants. The present work encompasses this topic, by proposing an IoT-based solution, relying on a commercial device, Airthings View 2960, to continuously monitor the pollutants present at the cellar level within the winemaking industry. The paper revolves around a proposal for Internet-of-Things-based architecture, allowing a seamless data exchange between the device and a control center remotely placed, with a description of the use case scenario and potential room for future improvements and refinements.

Título: Management of Safety-Critical AI Services in the Compute Continuum
Autores: Colombi, Lorenzo and Tortonesi, Mauro
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 21st International Conference on Network and Service Management (CNSM)
Abstract: The increasing complexity and criticality of AIdriven services across the compute continuum, spanning from edge devices to cloud datacenters, necessitates resilient, intelligent, and explainable management strategies. This work addresses the challenges of deploying and orchestrating safetycritical AI services in dynamic and resource-constrained environments, such as Industry 5.0 and Human Assistance and Disaster Recovery (HADR). We present a suite of complementary solutions, including a cloud-native MLOps platform tailored for SMEs, a semi-supervised federated learning framework (FedEdge-Learn), and novel semantic communication mechanisms that optimize data transmission using LLM-driven embeddings. Furthermore, we introduce an intent-based Zerotouch Service Management (ZSM) architecture, leveraging neurosymbolic AI and collaborative intelligence to automate orchestration, model fine-tuning, and policy reasoning across federated Kubernetes clusters. These efforts pave the way for trustworthy, adaptive, and efficient AI service lifecycle management in environments characterized by disconnections, privacy constraints, and operational unpredictability. Future work focuses on extending the neuro-symbolic approach to support additional tasks, including dynamic node selection, optimized placement across the compute continuum with the goal of improving resilience and interpretability in distributed, resource-constrained environments like Industry 5.0 and HADR, while addressing challenges such as intermittent connectivity and evolving operational conditions.

Título: Unleashing the Potential of Industrial IoT and Industry 5.0
Autores: Maurya, Poonam and Hazra, Abhishek and Kalita, Alakesh
Abstract: The transition to Industry 5.0 emphasizes the need and importance of human–machine collaboration, driving the demand for intelligent Internet of Things (IoT) and communication protocols. This paper examines the essential prerequisites for Industry 5.0, evaluates the existing constraints of IoT communication protocols, and highlights the requirements for industrial convergence. Specifically, the article focuses on and discusses the role of IoT protocols and standards in realizing the key objectives of Industry 5.0 over Industry 4.0. In addition, it outlines a human-centric Industry 5.0 reference architecture designed to support managers and decision-makers through real-time data visibility, predictive maintenance insights, and resource optimization. To this end, we introduce an edge-enabled Industry 5.0 reference architecture and use cases, particularly emphasizing the enhancement of human–machine interaction. This paper also examines the 6TiSCH (IPv6 over the Time-Slotted Channel Hopping mode of IEEE 802.15.4e) wireless network protocol, focusing on its performance evaluation, prospective advantages, and upcoming advancements. Finally, several open research challenges and managerial implications are discussed to achieve Industry 5.0 resolution.

Título: Design of Voice Based Security Protocol For IoT-Driven AI-Enabled Industry 5.0
Autores: Thapliyal, Siddhant and Wazid, Mohammad and Singh, D P
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Secure Engineering Solutions (CISES)
Abstract: The advent of Industry 5.0 has resulted in a seamless merger of human creativity with machine intelligence, propelling new levels of automation and innovation. Within this paradigm, the Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning (ML) are critical technologies that enable smart and adaptable industrial processes. However, increased connectivity and data interchange across IoT devices expose Industry 5.0 systems to a wide range of security vulnerabilities, including data breaches and adversarial assaults on ML models. This study presents a strong security framework designed for IoT-driven, machine learning-enabled settings in Industry 5.0. The protocol uses sophisticated encryption technologies, blockchain-based data integrity verification, and federated learning approaches to improve data privacy and system resilience. Furthermore, it uses anomaly detection methods to detect and mitigate real-time threats. A thorough study of the proposed protocol proves its capacity to provide data confidentiality, integrity, and availability while being computationally efficient. This study is an important step toward creating safe and trustworthy Industry 5.0 ecosystems.

Título: Fostering Industry 5.0 through Engineering Innovation: A Framework for Enhancing Creativity, Problem-Solving, and Early-Stage Technical Competency in Future Engineers
Autores: Leong, Wai Yie
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Computation, Big-Data and Engineering (ICCBE)
Abstract: The global engineering landscape transitions toward Industry 5.0, characterized by human-centric automation, hyper-customization, and sustainable co-creation. Therefore, it is needed to reconfigure educational paradigms to educate engineers to be equipped with advanced creativity, transdisciplinary problem-solving, and foundational technical acumen. In this study, a framework was developed, leveraging design-driven engineering innovation platforms, such as structured design fairs, to embed Industry 5.0 principles into undergraduate and early-career engineering curricula. Anchored in cyber-physical frameworks integration, digital twin modeling, and human-machine collaborative intelligence, the framework operationalizes experiential learning cycles to promote ideation, rapid prototyping, and frameworkic validation under real-world constraints. The framework is grounded in established engineering epistemologies, incorporating Bloom’s revised taxonomy for cognitive development, TRIZ-based methodologies for creative problem-solving, and ABET-aligned frameworks for assessing technical competencies. Empirical validation of the framework was conducted through multi-site intervention studies involving 320 engineering students. Metrics were used to assess computational thinking, embedded frameworks design, sustainability heuristics, and collaborative intelligence in pre- and post-intervention. The results indicated significant improvements in students’ abilities to decompose complex problems, demonstrate proficiency in digital fabrication, and apply frameworks engineering principles effectively. The results also presented the potential of innovation-driven educational interventions for advancing Industry 5.0 readiness. Such interventions help to solve the cognitive and technical divide between academic instruction and industrial application. The developed framework integrates ethical, innovative, and human-centric competencies into the curricula, enhancing educational outcomes to meet industrial demands.

Título: Eco-Innovation in Industry 5.0: Enablers, Barriers, and Future Directions for Sustainable Manufacturing
Autores: Enriquez, James and Delgado, Daniel Ricardo and Herrera, Cesar and Rincón-Guio, Cristian
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE Technology and Engineering Management Society (TEMSCON LATAM)
Abstract: The transition to Industry $\mathbf{5. 0}$ highlights the critical role of eco-innovation in achieving sustainable and resilient manufacturing systems. This study conducts a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis to explore the integration of digitalisation, regulatory frameworks, and organisational capabilities in eco-innovation adoption. Findings indicate that knowledge management, strategic orientation, and stakeholder collaboration are key enablers, while financial barriers and inconsistent regulations hinder adoption, particularly for SMEs. Moreover, emerging technologies such as AI, IoT, and circular economy strategies are reshaping sustainability practices in manufacturing. Despite growing research in this domain, gaps persist in sectorspecific applications and the harmonisation of global policies. The study provides insights for policymakers and industry leaders, offering a roadmap for scaling sustainable innovations. Future research should address sector-specific challenges, the role of digital sustainability tools, and the impact of regulatory frameworks to accelerate the adoption of sustainable Industry 5.0 models.

Título: Sustainable Industry 5.0 and Digital Transformation: Analytical Insights on Challenges, AI-Driven Strategies, Frameworks, and Future Directions
Autores: Yadavalli, Ramu and Sumeet, Anika
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 2nd International Conference on New Frontiers in Communication, Automation, Management and Security (ICCAMS)
Abstract: Digital transformation has advanced beyond the automation-centric principles of Industry 4.0 to embrace the human-centric, AI-driven vision of Industry 5.0, which emphasizes adaptability, sustainability, and intelligent collaboration. This study conducts an in-depth literature review of 20 key research articles, synthesizing the current trends, methodologies, and challenges shaping the evolution of Industry 5.0. A comparative analysis is performed between traditional and AI-enhanced digital transformation approaches, highlighting innovations in AI-based decision-making, edge computing, IoT integration, and data interoperability. To address persistent challenges, a comprehensive framework is proposed for a sustainable Industry 5.0 ecosystem that leverages AI, energy-efficient infrastructure, and scalable digital technologies. The study identifies emerging themes such as ethical AI governance, real-time analytics, and the transition toward resilient, decentralized infrastructures. A significant contribution is the structured integration of AI-driven automation, sustainable digital frameworks, and Industry 5.0 readiness. The findings offer a strategic direction for future research, supporting innovation, policy alignment, and industrial adoption of next-generation digital transformation models.

Título: Are We Measuring What Matters? Reframing Evaluation of Extended Reality for Industry 5.0 Work Environments
Autores: Ghafoori, Miran and Premsankar, Gopika and Tu, Xinyi
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE International Symposium on Mixed and Augmented Reality Adjunct (ISMAR-Adjunct)
Abstract: Current approaches to evaluating extended reality (XR) systems in industrial settings are narrowly focused on usability, device performance, or user experience, while overlooking broader systemic impacts. We argue that this limited scope is misaligned with the challenges and values of future workspaces. As XR technologies become more integrated into manufacturing and training environments, evaluation methods must expand to reflect the principles of Industry 5.0: human-centricity, sustainability, and resilience. In this position paper, we propose a multi-dimensional evaluation framework that incorporates task-technology fit alongside environmental, human, and operational criteria. The proposed framework enables structured, phase-specific assessment of XR systems to guide responsible deployment and adoption. We call on the XR research community to shift from fragmented metrics toward holistic evaluation practices that ensure XR contributes to more efficient, equitable, regenerative, and future-ready work environments.

Título: Hazardous Workplaces and the Role of VR in Stress Mitigation
Autores: Pulcini, Valerio and Modoni, Gianfranco
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE International Symposium on Mixed and Augmented Reality Adjunct (ISMAR-Adjunct)
Abstract: Workers in hazardous and extreme environments, such as confined spaces, offshore platforms, or isolated ICE (Isolated, Confined, and Extreme) settings, face significant physical, physiological, and psychological stressors that threaten performance, safety, and long-term well-being. This short survey, inspired by Industry 5.0’s human-centered principles, categorizes the main sources of strain in these workplaces and examines their immediate and lasting impacts on health and productivity. It then explores how Virtual Reality (VR) technologies can help mitigate these challenges through immersive simulations, targeted psychological training, and real-time remote support. By integrating VR into preparation and ongoing operations, organizations can foster safer, more supportive workplaces that prioritize both performance excellence and the dignity, mental health, and resilience of workers.

Título: Advancing Industry 5.0 with IoT Transformations: Future Prospectives
Autores: Tunwal, Bhawna and Kaur, Amandeep and Kumar, Sudesh
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 International Conference on Next Generation of Green Information and Emerging Technologies (GIET)
Abstract: The recent convergence of the Internet of Things (IoT) and Industry 5.0 has resulted in a new paradigm in contemporary industrial and manufacturing systems. This paradigm emphasizes the seamless integration of cutting-edge technology with human talents. The IoT lays the framework for intelligent automation, connection, and real-time data collection. At the same time, Industry 5.0 strongly emphasizes people by prioritizing customization and resilience. This article aims to investigate the synergistic integration of the IoT with Industry 5.0, stressing IoT's critical role in Industry 5.0. The research investigates essential applications such as managing supply chains, monitoring health, developing novel educational practices, collaborating with humans and robots, and human-centric smart manufacturing. In addition, it discusses the challenges and presents a roadmap for future research directions in which technology will complement rather than replace the human workforce.

Título: Integrating IoT Sensors and Data Analytics to Optimize the Sustainable Production Routing Problem in Industry 5.0
Autores: Garside, Annisa Kesy and Muhtazaruddin, Mohd Nabil and Ahmad, Robiah and Yusoff, Nelidya Md and Mad Kaidi, Hazilah and Sarip, Shamsul
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE 11th International Conference on Smart Instrumentation, Measurement and Applications (ICSIMA)
Abstract: This study presents a conceptual framework that integrates Internet of Things (IoT) sensors and data analytics into the Sustainable Production Routing Problem (SUPRP), aligning with Industry 5.0 principles. The framework enables real-time parameter estimation by processing sensor data through descriptive and predictive analytics, capturing dynamic conditions such as cost, emissions, and safety risks. These estimated parameters serve as inputs to a multi-objective optimization model solved using exact or metaheuristic methods. Compared to static approaches, the proposed architecture supports adaptive and sustainability-oriented decision-making across production and distribution planning. While implementation is left for future work, the framework provides a structured foundation for real-world applications in smart manufacturing and logistics.

Título: Redesigning Supply Chains for Industry 5.0 in Developing Economies: A Research Agenda
Autores: Bandara, Amila and Thibbotuwawa, Amila and Perera, H. Niles
Abstract: Unlike the previous industry revolutions that were predominantly focused on enhancing the efficiency of industrial systems, Industry $\mathbf{5. 0}$ (I5.0) aims at transforming global industries to become more sustainable, resilient, and human-centric. This paper brings a much-needed developing economy perspective to the debate on the interplay between $\mathbf{5. 0}$ and supply chain (SC). A sample of 89 peer-reviewed journal articles was selected from SCOPUS and Web of Science databases through a systematic literature review. The network co-occurrence diagram revealed three prominent research clusters, namely: SC Process Improvement, SC Resilience, and SC Sustainability. Research gap analysis revealed several future research directions: Promoting the adoption of $\mathbf{1 5. 0}$ in Developing Economies, Human-centered SCs, Emerging technology applications Strategy roadmaps to adopt I5.0, and $\mathbf{I 5. 0}$ certification and compliance. These directions can be used by future researchers, industries and intergovernmental organizations to streamline their efforts to popularize $\mathbf{1 5. 0}$ in SCs operating at developing economies.

Título: Exploring Industry 4.0 and 5.0 Technologies: a Systematic Review of Emerging Transitions and Applications
Autores: Belgada, Khira and El Abbadi, Laila
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE 8th Congress on Information Science and Technology (CiSt)
Abstract: With the emergence of Industry 4.0 and 5.0, industrial ecosystems are undergoing profound transformations. This study provides a systematic review of the literature to analyze the technological, human, and environmental dimensions of these paradigms. Using Kitchenham's methodological model and the VOSviewer bibliometric tool, 56 articles were examined. The results highlight the convergence of advanced technologies (digital twins, blockchain, augmented reality) with the challenges of sustainability and human-centered innovation. While Industry 4.0 emphasizes automation and intelligent systems, Industry 5.0 introduces a new dynamic based on human-machine collaboration and ethical values. This summary identifies key technologies and major challenges and proposes concrete avenues for future research.

Título: Cognitive Cells and Human-Robot Interaction in Industry 5.0: an Overview
Autores: Amorim, Ivan and Lopes, Sérgio Ivan
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE 8th Congress on Information Science and Technology (CiSt)
Abstract: Industry 5.0 (I5.0) builds on the foundations of Industry 4.0 (I4.0) by placing greater emphasis on human centricity, collaboration, and adaptability within industrial systems. Although I4.0 has focused on efficiency and automation, it has often overlooked critical dimensions such as human well-being, creativity, and sustainability. I5.0 aims to bridge this gap by merging human capabilities with AI, IoT, and adaptive control to foster intelligent, responsive, and inclusive production environments. This paper makes two main contributions. First, it provides an overview of the current literature on cognitive cells and human-robot interaction in the context of Industry 5.0, identifying key trends, challenges, and enabling technologies. Second, it introduces the conceptual architecture for a human-aware cognitive cell that integrates perception, behavioral adaptation, ergonomic feedback, and collaborative robotic execution. This architecture aims to demonstrate how human-machine co-creation can be effectively supported in real-world manufacturing environments, contributing to the broader vision of a human-centric and resilient industrial future.

Título: Startups in the Era of Industry 4.0 and 5.0: Technologies, Decisions, Framing, and Competences
Autores: Romano, André Luiz and Henrique Dos Santos, Carlos and Koch, Christoph and Lourenço Ubeda, Cristina and Rorato Fogaça, Diego and César Almada Santos, Fernando and Freitas, Vérica
Abstract: This article investigates the evolving domain of Startup 4.0/5.0, which leverages advanced Industry 4.0 and 5.0 technologies to support startups’ processes and activities. As startups face increasing complexity and competitiveness, understanding how digital innovations and emerging approaches contribute to improved performance, agility, and innovation becomes essential. Through a systematic literature review of peer-reviewed articles published up to December 2024, this study maps the current research landscape. The review responds to key research questions related to business sectors, applied tools, decision objectives, conceptual framings, and required skills and competences. Findings reveal a growing yet still underexplored field, with multidisciplinary relevance and a concentration of research in countries like Brazil and Germany, spanning sectors such as Advanced Manufacturing, Agrotech, Healthcare, and Education. Most reviewed works emphasize technical, managerial, and market-oriented perspectives, focusing on productivity and competitiveness, while elements central to Industry 5.0, such as sustainability, human-centric design, and resilience, remain marginal, appearing in few studies. Decision objectives were classified into key areas, including innovation, sustainability, digital transformation, and interinstitutional collaboration, highlighting the strategic role of digital technologies in business model redesign and ecosystem development. Moreover, the review identifies critical competences required for professionals in Startup 4.0/5.0 contexts, organizing several core competences into personal, social, and cultural categories and linking them to specific technologies, aiming to inform workforce training and behavioral change. By synthesizing these insights, the article contributes to a deeper theoretical understanding of Startup 4.0/5.0 and offers practical implications for this field.

Título: From Silos to Synergy: A Serious Game for Cross-Functional Collaboration in Human-Centric Asset Management
Autores: Barbieri, Giacomo and Zapata, Freddy
Abstract: Asset Management (AM) is an integrative discipline that relies on expert knowledge from diverse functions to develop holistic and coordinated solutions. However, the necessary division of responsibilities within and across organizations often leads to the formation of silos—isolated departments or teams that hinder communication and collaboration, ultimately undermining AM’s integrative nature. To address this challenge, a Serious Game (SG), From Silos to Synergy, was developed in this work. Guided by a Research through Design approach—where knowledge develops through iterative experimentation and the creation of artifacts—the SG aims to foster reflection on the relational and organizational dimensions of AM, thereby enabling the definition of cross-functional collaboration as a foundation of Human-Centric Asset Management (HuCAM). Grounded in a family finance analogy, the game integrates frameworks from AM, Industry 5.0, and game-based learning, underwent three design iterations, and was tested with 31 master’s students and 119 practitioners. The results indicate that the SG generated two main outcomes. On the one hand, it led to the creation of a Maturity Model for Cross-Functional Collaboration in HuCAM, offering a structured framework to evaluate and guide the transition toward more collaborative and human-centric AM practices. On the other hand, it fostered cultural awareness in cross-functional collaboration by challenging silo thinking and enhancing players’ understanding of the strategic and collaborative dimensions of AM. By promoting long-term value creation and human-centric thinking, From Silos to Synergy provides a practical and engaging pathway for developing the mindset and capabilities needed to tackle the complex, dynamic, and interdependent challenges of sustainability and resilience in modern asset systems.

texto_completo: From Silos to Synergy: A Serious Game for Cross-Functional Collaboration in Human-Centric Asset Management Asset Management (AM) is an integrative discipline that relies on expert knowledge from diverse functions to develop holistic and coordinated solutions. However, the necessary division of responsibilities within and across organizations often leads to the formation of silos—isolated departments or teams that hinder communication and collaboration, ultimately undermining AM’s integrative nature. To address this challenge, a Serious Game (SG), From Silos to Synergy, was developed in this work. Guided by a Research through Design approach—where knowledge develops through iterative experimentation and the creation of artifacts—the SG aims to foster reflection on the relational and organizational dimensions of AM, thereby enabling the definition of cross-functional collaboration as a foundation of Human-Centric Asset Management (HuCAM). Grounded in a family finance analogy, the game integrates frameworks from AM, Industry 5.0, and game-based learning, underwent three design iterations, and was tested with 31 master’s students and 119 practitioners. The results indicate that the SG generated two main outcomes. On the one hand, it led to the creation of a Maturity Model for Cross-Functional Collaboration in HuCAM, offering a structured framework to evaluate and guide the transition toward more collaborative and human-centric AM practices. On the other hand, it fostered cultural awareness in cross-functional collaboration by challenging silo thinking and enhancing players’ understanding of the strategic and collaborative dimensions of AM. By promoting long-term value creation and human-centric thinking, From Silos to Synergy provides a practical and engaging pathway for developing the mindset and capabilities needed to tackle the complex, dynamic, and interdependent challenges of sustainability and resilience in modern asset systems.

Título: Adaptive Digital Twin Systems with AR Interaction for Resilient and Sustainable Industrial Operations
Autores: Gayathri, G. and Fathima, G.
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 6th International Conference on Electronics and Sustainable Communication Systems (ICESC)
Abstract: The integration of Augmented Reality (AR) with Digital Twin (DT) technology is increasingly recognized as a transformative approach for achieving resilient and sustainable industrial operations. This research presents an Adaptive Digital Twin (DT) framework integrated with Augmented Reality (AR) to enhance resilience, predictive intelligence, and sustainability in industrial operations. The proposed Immersive Sensing Digital Twin (ImmersiSense-Twin) algorithm combines real-time 3D point cloud acquisition, multimodal sensor fusion, and edge-deployed artificial intelligence to deliver immersive, context-aware operational insights. The system architecture leverages low-latency edge processing and AR-based visualization to facilitate rapid anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, and resource optimization in dynamic industrial environments. Simulation experiments were conducted using industrial time-series datasets in a controlled digital twin simulation testbed. Performance was evaluated against three benchmark algorithms: Deep Embedded Clustering (DEC), LSTM-Autoencoder for Industrial Time-Series (LSTM-AE), and Federated Learning-Based Predictive Maintenance Model (FedPM). The comparison was based on prediction accuracy, anomaly detection rate, latency, resource utilization efficiency, and AR rendering time. The ImmersiSense-Twin algorithm achieved notable improvements, including up to 9.3% higher prediction accuracy, 12.5% faster anomaly detection, and 14.8% better resource utilization efficiency compared to the best-performing baseline. The results validate the suitability of the proposed framework for Industry 4.0 and emerging Industry 5.0 environments, offering a pathway toward more resilient, intelligent, and sustainable industrial ecosystems. The findings demonstrate that the integration of adaptive DT systems with immersive AR interaction provides significant operational advantages, enabling proactive decision-making and reducing downtime in mission-critical industrial applications.

Título: Towards a Digital Twin-Based Evaluation Framework for Cyber-Physical Production Systems: Latin America SMEs Guideline
Autores: Chacón, Edgar and Cruz Salazar, Luis Alberto and Cruz, Ernesto Monroy and Valdez-Cervantes, Libis and Sánchez-Gómez, Juan Sebastián and Larrondo-Petrie, Maria Mercedes
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE 30th International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)
Abstract: The evaluation of Cyber-Physical Production Systems (CPPS) using Digital Twin (DT) architectures and Asset Administration Shells (AAS) is critical for advancing flexible, autonomous, and human-centric manufacturing environments. However, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), particularly in Latin America, face significant barriers to adopting and evaluating these technologies due to resource limitations, complexity, and lack of standardized frameworks. This paper proposes a scalable and modular evaluation framework specifically designed for SMEs, integrating DTs for real-time simulation and monitoring, AAS for semantic interoperability, and simulation-based assessment methods to measure CPPS autonomy, flexibility, and resilience. A comprehensive review of recent approaches, trends, challenges, and research gaps highlights the urgent need for dynamic, standardized, and cognitive-enabled evaluation methodologies. The proposed framework addresses these needs by formalizing production knowledge through ontologies, synchronizing physical systems with digital models, and enabling systematic performance evaluation across diverse production scenarios. A case study conducted in a Latin American manufacturing SME demonstrates the practical application of the framework, showing improvements in production efficiency, decision transparency, and system adaptability. The results underline the framework’s potential to democratize access to advanced Industry 4.0 solutions for SMEs, fostering more resilient and intelligent manufacturing ecosystems. By bridging current technological gaps, this work contributes to accelerating the digital transformation of SMEs and supports the broader goals of Industry 5.0. Future research will explore the integration of explainable AI techniques and expand the framework’s applicability to multi-site production networks.

Título: Technology Embedded Transformative Potential in Sustainability Reporting: Business Impacts and Innovations
Autores: Sharma, Ravi and Kunwar, Harshvardhan
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 International Conference on Technology Enabled Economic Changes (InTech)
Abstract: This study conducts a systematic literature review based on the PRISMA technique to investigate the transformation of technology on sustainability practices, disclosures and reporting. The documents were collected from Scopus and Web of Science research databases. The results highlighted Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Industry 5.0. Through secure and auditable data trails, particularly in the context of supply chain management, Blockchain makes data more reliable and transparent. Data collection and realtime reporting are automated, with AI and machine learning driving the materiality assessments. In addition to the Industry 4.0 practices, Industry 5.0 principles would enhance individual and real-time ESG reporting by making it customisable and cost-efficient, promoting greater stakeholder participation, and allowing more meaningful inter-company comparability. Using a structured literature review approach and integrating with empirical analysis like principal component analysis and K-mean clustering using Ward's method, the results and discussion outline technological advances that aim to solve essential sustainability reporting-related challenges by providing uniform methods and fostering stakeholder confidence. These research findings have implications for practitioners and policymakers on leveraging technologies effectively to enhance sustainability reporting.

Título: Enhancing Industrial Processes Through Digital Twin Technology in the Era of Industry 5.0
Autores: Prathiba, Sahaya Beni and R., Dhanalakshmi and Kumar, Suraj and Kumar, Sawan and Kumar, Abhishek
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 International Conference on Technology Enabled Economic Changes (InTech)
Abstract: Industry 5.0 broadens the scope of digital twins' application beyond performance and production augmenting as it demands advanced human-machine interface symbiosis with AI, Cyber Physical Systems, augmented reality, and sustainable resilient technologies. It seeks to evaluate the effectiveness of DT technology on industrial manufacturing constructs with real-time process performance evaluation, error identification, and correction at its core. The study investigates the major modeling techniques, active uses, and the role of DT in the acceleration of automated real-time process monitoring and error supervision and correction for achieving greater efficiencies and lower operational costs in industrial manufacturing. It seeks to demonstrate the ability of Industry 5.0 technologies to fundamentally change industrial practices and processes, enhance productivity, flexibility, operational efficiency, and resilience through humancentered manufacturing practice with digital twins. This will demonstrate the ability of DT to transform the next stage of industrial revolution endeavors.

Título: Towards Engineering Product Digital Twins for Industry 5.0: Definition and Modeling Approach
Autores: Nguyen, Quang-Duy and Suri, Kunal and Sidibe, Guéréguin Der Sylvestre
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE 30th International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)
Abstract: The vision of Industry 5.0 builds upon the advanced technologies of Industry 4.0, aligning its emerging concepts with three key pillars: human-centricity, sustainability, and resilience. In this context, the idea of the Product Digital Twin (PDT), first introduced in 2002, which has further matured (and refined) by the Asset Administration Shell (AAS) standard, must continue evolving to integrate the vision of Digital Product Passport (DPP) as promoted via several initiatives from the European Commission. Moreover, positioning PDT correctly within this broader context of Industry 5.0 is crucial, as it involves the modeling and implementation of PDT instances, which then significantly influence manufacturing applications. To address this need, this paper first harmonizes different PDT definitions and then proposes a modeling and deployment approach appropriate to the new concept of PDT information models.

Título: Securing IoE Environments with Semantic Data Stream Analysis and Behavioral Fingerprinting
Autores: Arazzi, Marco and Sciarroni, Monica Marconi and Nicolazzo, Serena and Nocera, Antonino and Storti, Emanuele
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE 30th International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)
Abstract: In the landscape of Industry 5.0, Internet of Everything (IoE) networks are emerging as crucial components for connecting diverse industrial sensors and devices, expanding beyond traditional IoT boundaries to integrate people, processes, and data. However, this increased connectivity raises significant security concerns, as the growing complexity of IoE environments introduces new attack vectors and privacy risks. Additionally, the integration of heterogeneous devices and data sources presents both technical and semantic interoperability challenges, requiring robust mechanisms for meaningful data interpretation and secure exchange. This paper, developed within the HOMEY project, presents an architecture for gathering and monitoring semantic data streams in IoE environments, addressing both interoperability and security challenges. Our approach leverages Knowledge Graphs to represent sensor metadata, locations, access rights, and operational contexts, enabling dynamic stream monitoring and data querying. An approach based on Federated Learning allows distributed behavioral fingerprinting of IoE devices, which is exploited on top of the platform to perform anomaly detection from real-time data streams. The approach enhances reliable, privacy-preserving anomaly detection, contributing to the security and resilience of next-generation industrial IoE ecosystems.

Título: An Improved Hybrid Approach for Proactive Healthcare Industry Risk Prediction: Integrating Graph Weighted Fusion, RF and RW-GCN
Autores: Bi, KeJun and Liu, ChuanJie and Dai, Cheng and Guo, Bing and Politis, Ilias
Jornal/Conferência: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
Abstract: Risk prediction in healthcare industrial chains is critical for ensuring operational resilience and systemic stability. Traditional methods often focus on supply chain topology while overlooking enterprise-level indicators and the complex interdependencies among participants. To address these limitations, we propose IA-GWRG, a hybrid framework that integrates multi-relational graph modeling, key indicator selection, and subgraph-level learning for fine-grained enterprise risk prediction. Designed to align with emerging 6G-enabled intelligent infrastructures, IA-GWRG leverages ultra-low latency and ubiquitous sensing to enable real-time risk awareness. First, we introduce a salient graph feature extraction method that transforms a multi-relational industrial chain graph into a homogeneous structure using weighted fusion based on “competition–supply” meta-paths. A local-global-positional scheme is then applied to capture multi-scale structural features. Second, a key indicator identification module constructs a domain-specific 26-dimensional risk system and employs a random forest algorithm to select the most informative micro-level indicators, enhancing interpretability and reducing feature noise. Third, a node risk assessment method combines selected indicators and structural embeddings via subgraph-level random walk sampling and GCN-based learning, enabling precise and context-aware risk prediction. Extensive experiments on real-world healthcare industry chain datasets demonstrate that IA-GWRG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across multiple metrics. The results confirm its effectiveness and robustness in both predictive accuracy and 6G-oriented deployment scenarios.

Título: A Multimodal Emotion Recognition Enhanced Resilient Cognitive Twin
Autores: Ge, Chenyu and Qin, Shengfeng
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 30th International Conference on Automation and Computing (ICAC)
Abstract: In next-generation engineered systems, particularly those involving complex interactions among cyber, physical, and socio-technical components, human intelligence (HI), as a "human-in-the-loop" element, needs to play a critical role in ensuring the system resilience and right-decision making under unforeseen and uncertain evolving conditions. Although predefined artificial intelligence (AI) models can offer some decision support for predefined problems, but due to its limited explainability, HI is still key to decision adaption/adoption. However, HI’s cognition and judgment are inevitably influenced by a subject’s emotional states, especially when unforeseen emergency situations happen in complex cyber-physical-social environments. To address this challenge, this study presents a critical review of Human-Cyber-Physical System (HCPS)’s resilience challenges and accordingly proposes a Multimodal Emotion Recognition enhanced Resilient Cognitive Twin (MER-RCT) of a HCPS and its three major mechanisms in addressing the system resilience. This MER-RCT not only supports the generation, interaction, and integration of human and artificial cognition and decisions under situation awareness but also incorporates emotion-aware capabilities to reflect the evolution of human affective states under situational awareness. By embedding near-real-time MER into the situational awareness and decision-support processes, the proposed MER-RCT enhances the emotional and cognitive resilience of HCPS during emergencies. A prototype MER-RCT system is validated through a flood emergency scenario, demonstrating its feasibility in distributed, uncertain environments.

Título: Improved Carnivorous Plant Algorithm for Human–Robot Collaborative U-Shaped Disassembly Line Balancing With Mobile Workers
Autores: Qin, Shujin and Dai, Shaokang and Wang, Jiacun and Liu, Shixin and Guo, Xiwang and Qi, Liang and Hu, Bin and Ji, Yingjun
Jornal/Conferência: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems
Abstract: The advancement of human–robot collaboration technology has positioned remanufacturing as a crucial part of the circular economy, driving both economic growth and environmental sustainability. In the era of Industry 5.0, these technologies enhance the efficiency and flexibility of disassembly tasks. However, most research on human–robot collaborative disassembly (HRCD) line balancing overlooks the mobility of workers. This study introduces a profit-oriented HRCD model incorporating mobile workers. To address large-scale HRCD challenges, it proposes a dynamic attraction rate mechanism that improves the traditional carnivorous plant algorithm (CPA), tackling issues of slow convergence and local optimization. The experimental framework includes three validation phases: 1) comparison with the exact solver IBM ILOG CPLEX Optimization Studio (CPLEX); 2) parameter sensitivity analysis; and 3) benchmarking against seven state-of-the-art algorithms. Results demonstrate that HRCD with mobile workers significantly boosts disassembly efficiency and reduces disassembly time compared to traditional methods. Additionally, it increases profits through flexible task allocation. In cases of incomplete disassembly, HRCD with mobile workers yields an average benefit increase of 87.64% over conventional disassembly modes. A comparative evaluation with other swarm intelligence algorithms further highlights the superior solution quality and time efficiency of the improved CPA.

Título: Boosting Trustworthiness in 6G-Enabled Smart Industries 5.0 through Explainable Artificial Intelligence on Industrial Machine Anomaly Data
Autores: Jing, Hengchang and Huang, Lijia
Abstract: New industrial paradigms, like Industry 5.0 and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), are developing in industrial contexts with the objective of foster quality. The growth of 6G-enabled smart industries requires interpretable, secure, and adaptive anomaly detection structures able to operate under adversarial, dynamic, and resource-constrained environments. Inappropriately, the usage of these technologies, successively, strengthens the attacking surface and poses a significant attack to the novel goals of Industry 5.0, like enhancing the user experience, resilience, and sustainability. In this setting, human-machine collaboration and cyber-physical integration request that anomaly detection systems surpass only prediction and include resilience, interpretability, and scalability. Traditional anomaly detection systems in Industry 4.0, like machine learning (ML)-based detection show remarkable challenges. These contain vulnerability to antagonistic attacks owing to vulnerable updates of the model, rigidity in adjusting to concept and temporal drift, and unclear decision processes that hamper trust and accountability. Therefore, this study develops an explainable artificial intelligence with a feature selection strategy enabled anomaly detection (XAIFSS-AD) technique for improving trustworthiness in 6G driven smart industry 5.0. The primary objective is to unravel the security issues in the smart industry environment via the anomaly identification process with the XAI approach to elaborate the proposed model. The presented XAIFSS-AD technique involves data scaling using a robust scalar which uses median and interquartile range to standardize the network data. In addition, the selection of features can be performed using the recursive feature elimination (RFE) process to eliminate the least significant features and enhance the classification process. A variational autoencoder with attention bidirectional long short-term memory (VAE-ABiLSTM) is deployed for anomaly detection. The performance of the classification model can be fine-tuned by Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) which optimally chooses the hyperparameter values. Finally, the Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) methodology is applied to offer descriptions of the presented methods. The performance of the XAIFSS-AD approach is evaluated utilizing the benchmark datasets. The outcomes specify that the proposed model surpasses the other inspected systems and advanced models.

A variational autoencoder with attention bidirectional long short-term memory (VAE-ABiLSTM) is deployed for anomaly detection. The performance of the classification model can be fine-tuned by Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) which optimally chooses the hyperparameter values. Finally, the Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) methodology is applied to offer descriptions of the presented methods. The performance of the XAIFSS-AD approach is evaluated utilizing the benchmark datasets. The outcomes specify that the proposed model surpasses the other inspected systems and advanced models.

Título: Industry 5.0: Advancing a Research Agenda at the Intersection of Sustainability and Human-Centricity Enabled through Technology
Autores: Parthasarathy, Rangarajan and Olcay, Gokcen Arkali and Rangarajan, Anuradha

Abstract: Industry 5.0 marks a transformative shift from Industry 4.0, emphasizing sustainability, human-centricity, and resilience, with technology as a key enabler. This scoping review explores these pillars and their interconnected roles in shaping the future of industry. Sustainability encompasses economic, environmental, and social dimensions, ensuring long-term viability. Human-centricity focuses on designing human-in-theloop workflows, addressing cognitive biases, ethics, fears, psychological and social factors, emerging human-centric risks, and evolving industry roles and skills. Technologies such as cobots and cognitive artificial intelligence serve as foundational enablers, enhancing production efficiency, resource optimization, and product quality. Resilience in Industry 5.0 is an expected outcome that follows from the strategic integration of sustainability and human-centricity, enabled by advanced technology. This paper highlights the critical role of these elements in fostering a more adaptive, efficient, and human-friendly industrial ecosystem. As a next step in our ongoing research, we plan to develop and test a model involving supply chain management within the Industry 5.0 framework.

Título: Efficient and Human Centered Industry 5.0 Data Propagation on the Operational Technology Level. Case Study with OPC UA Interfacing, Node-RED and Ignition
Autores: Korodi, Adrian and Vesa, Vlad-Cristian and Dontu, Raul-Andrei
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE 21st International Conference on Automation Science and Engineering (CASE)
Abstract: Industry 5.0 is focused on human centricity, sustainability and resilience, but in the meantime it is relying on Industry 4.0 main objective that refers to efficiency increase. The operational technology (OT) level usually lacks data structuring and context, these steps being attributed to the middleware interfacing with the information technology (IT), or higher SCADA levels. Higher the hierarchical level, lower the technological process related knowledge becomes, and therefore representations may not be optimal. Also, various supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) solutions development targeting the same controlled process lead to different perspectives, higher costs, larger development times, and a more difficult maintenance. Considering both legacy systems and technological progress, the current paper proposes a solution that assures efficient and human centered structured, contextualized, and graphically sustained data propagation on the OT level. The work approaches and builds upon industry adopted environments and protocols in order to assure a fast adoption and a large impact of the solution. A Node-RED and Ignition based case study is presented, representing the PLC to SCADA data integration levels. The structured and graphically depicted data transfer and representation using Open Platform Communication Unified Architecture (OPC UA) protocol is showing good results, without the need of additional developments on the SCADA levels.

Título: PSDEEN: Predictive and Secured Decentralized Energy-Efficient 6G Edge Networks for Industrial Consumer Applications
Autores: Haseeb, Khalid and Rehman, Amjad and Singh, Sushil Kumar and Shafique, Ayesha and Mirdad, Abeer Rashad and Jiang, Weiwei
Abstract: In smart cities, the Internet of Things (IoT) has increased the development and expansion of communication processes for Industry 5.0. With the integration of edge computing, 6G networks offer dynamic and low-cost services for consumer-centric applications to improve problem-solving abilities. However, heterogeneous services face issues controlling massive traffic on restricted systems and transmission delays. Moreover, due to the limitations of advanced technologies for various constraints, embedded applications experience data management issues and consume additional energy for associated services. In this research, we proposed a predictive distributed energy-efficient edge protocol for consumer industrial systems with the support of trusted communication over the 6G networks. It improved the computation outcomes using intelligent and lightweight power resources for integrated devices. Furthermore, it offers traffic-aware and reliable green energy systems for mobile services, particularly in rural areas. By leveraging the 6G technology for high bandwidth and low latency, edge computing provides consumer data processing closer to IoT devices, enabling on-time, real-time decision-making. It includes load-balancing functionality and increases the sustainability level for industrial applications. Using simulations, significant improvement has been revealed to highlight the potential of the proposed protocol and support the demands of Industry 5.0 for round-trip time by 33%, energy consumption by 39%, end-to-end delay by 41%, and complexity detection 30% than existing work.

Título: LLM-Powered Operator Advisor for Human-Robot Collaboration in Sustainable Assembly-Disassembly Cells
Autores: Kheirabadi, Mahboobe and Ghorbani, Elham and Keivanpour, Samira
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Human-Machine Systems (ICHMS)
Abstract: In response to the manufacturing shift toward customization and human-centered approaches in Industry 5.0, this paper presents a conceptual framework for a virtual operator advisor based on the Large Language Model (LLM). The LLM-powered advisor processes real-time data from the assembly or disassembly line, classifying it into operational efficiency, ergonomics, and sustainability metrics to deliver context-aware, adaptive guidance tailored to each task. It is achieved by cross-referencing these data with domain knowledge stored in the database and LLM capabilities. The Advisor recommends actions toward operations optimization, potential cognitive and physical strains, and environmental responsibility. As a framework that promotes workflow adaptability, sustainability, and worker well-being, it can contribute to the evolution of human-robot collaboration in modern manufacturing.

Título: Speech Recognition Systems in Healthcare: A Journey Towards Transformation
Autores: Dutta, Debanwita and Raut, Anjana and Samantaray, Swati and Roy, Aviroop
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 International Conference on Advancements in Smart, Secure and Intelligent Computing (ASSIC)
Abstract: The Industry 5.0 has the potential to leverage human-technology collaboration in fields like bionic and medical innovations, and is centered on developing completely automated, intelligent production systems that require little to no human involvement. The medical system may gain a great deal from the combination of sustainability, anti-fragile objectives, and digitization. Google Assistant, Amazon Alexa and Apple's Siri are the globally popular voice assistant software applications capable of integrating with AI powered smart devices. All these AI-modulated programs follow the basics of intelligent speech recognition. With the use of technology, we may now converse with an electronic computer or other equipment that will decode, interpret, and answer to our commands or questions. These artificial intelligence-modulated voice-controlled assistants have an extended past of growth and invention. However, it was their outsourcing into the voice recognition industry that fundamentally altered the way that technology is used in the twenty-first century. Digital assistants are rapidly replacing human help in many areas of life, so it is important for us to comprehend their capabilities and the many ways in which they can benefit individuals as well as organizations. The paper discusses the way Industry 5.0 seeks to transform healthcare by fusing state-of-the-art technology with sustainable practices, ultimately enhancing treatment outcomes and patient care.

Autores: Wang, Hao-Yi and Cheng, Chao-Tse and Lin, Hsiao-Fan and Su, Kuo-Wei
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 IEEE Gaming, Entertainment, and Media Conference (GEM)
Abstract: Wireless communication technologies have facilitated the effective network design and deployment of industrial IoT devices within manufacturing, assembly, and warehouse environments. These technologies significantly enhance productivity and efficiency by increasing manufacturing agility and customization capabilities, aligning closely with the goals of Industry 4.0. However, the growing complexity and heightened demands for customized production processes necessitate stronger human creativity and coordination skills. As we envision a future increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence, human-robot collaboration should strategically leverage inherent human strengths to form a co-evolutionary relationship. This study employs the Delphi method, design thinking, and affinity diagrams to explore warehouse operation scenarios that support assembly line processes. During the design and development phases, key design principles were proposed to achieve an Industry 5.0-oriented AR assistance system. Additionally, usability evaluations were conducted to gather authentic user experiences and validate the effectiveness of these proposed design principles.

Título: Artificial Intelligence for Supply Chain Sustainability: A Research Roadmap
Autores: Peeris, Maria Patricia and Baryannis, George
Jornal/Conferência: 2025 International Conference on Software, Knowledge, Information Management & Applications (SKIMA)
Abstract: In recent years, there has been an increasingly strong interest in improving supply chain sustainability to deal with wide-ranging impacts, from climate change to global trade uncertainty. While Artificial Intelligence has been identified as a key Industry 5.0 technology, its significant potential in the context of sustainability has not yet been harnessed. In this paper, we first present the results of a systematic literature review to both clarify the potential of AI for supply chain sustainability and understand which particular AI technologies have been utilised and for which application. Through insights drawn from this literature survey, we propose a research roadmap centred around four leading-edge AI approaches: generative AI, knowledge graphs, neurosymbolic AI and causal machine learning, and provide indicative suggestions for leveraging these approaches to help supply chain stakeholders meets sustainability targets.

Título: A Systematic Literature Review of Resilience Approaches in Production Systems
Autores: Hostos, Héctor and Goepp, Virginie and Sondi, Patrick
Abstract: The digitalization of industrial production systems through the Industry 4.0 paradigm has led to significant gains in efficiency and customization. However, it introduces new vulnerabilities, including heightened cybersecurity risks and increased dependence on network connectivity. Therefore, resilience emerges as a critical capability for maintaining operations and ensuring the recovery of production systems in the face of disruptions. This article presents a systematic literature review on resilience approaches in production systems, crucial for navigating the challenges of Industry 4.0. It adopts a three-perspective framework to analyze existing literature: resilience phases, resilience strategy decision space, and manufacturing system life cycle. The literature is classified into general frameworks, architectures, and methods, providing a structured overview of the field. The analysis reveals several key gaps, such as the need for practical implementation of resilience frameworks, the development of proactive strategies regarding the readiness phase, the exploration of underutilized areas in the resilience strategy decision space and the introduction of alternative resilience representations. The findings underscore the need to consider resilience, beyond a reaction to specific risks, as a broader capability to ensure the recovery of the production systems, and to open the path to new research directions.

Título: Robotic automation for sustainable and efficient egg poultry farming
Autores: Leong, Wai Yie
Jornal/Conferência: International Conference on Applied System Innovation (ICASI 2025)
Abstract: The integration of robotic automation in egg poultry farming has emerged as a transformative approach to enhancing productivity, sustainability, and animal welfare. This paper investigates the application of robotics in various aspects of egg poultry farming, including automated egg collection, sorting, health monitoring, environmental control, and feed management. By leveraging advanced robotics systems integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT), the proposed framework aims to optimize operational efficiency, minimize labor dependency, and enhance precision management in poultry farms. Key areas addressed include the development of autonomous robotic systems for continuous monitoring of environmental parameters such as temperature, humidity, and air quality, which are critical for maintaining optimal poultry health and egg production. The use of robotic manipulators for efficient and gentle egg collection and sorting minimizes breakage and ensures product quality. Machine learning algorithms embedded within robotic systems enable predictive maintenance and real-time decision-making, thus enhancing the resilience and robustness of poultry farming operations. This study explores the potential environmental benefits of robotic automation, particularly in reducing energy consumption, minimizing waste, and promoting ethical farming practices through improved animal welfare. Comparative analysis between traditional farming practices and robotic-assisted operations highlights substantial gains in productivity, precision, and sustainability. The findings highlight potential of robotics in modern poultry farming, advocating for further research and development to overcome existing challenges such as cost, scalability, and technological integration. This study provides a foundational basis for deploying robotic systems that contribute to the evolution of sustainable and efficient egg poultry farming under Industry 5.0 principles.

Título: Machine Learning for Industry 5.0: A Survey
Autores: Sarkar, Indranil and Kakarla, J. H. Hemanth and Hazra, Abhishek and Gupta, Krishna and Kumari, Preti and Munusamy, Ambigavathi
Abstract: Industry 5.0 represents a significant advancement from Industry 4.0, emphasizing improved cooperation between humans and machines, eco-friendly practices, and customized solutions in manufacturing. In contrast to earlier research on Industry 4.0, this survey provides a thorough examination of the function of machine learning (ML) in Industry 5.0 by examining the ways in which various learning paradigms facilitate sustainable production, human–machine cooperation, and customized industrial solutions. We first examine cutting-edge learning approaches, encompassing supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised, and reinforcement learning methodologies, and their role in advancing Industry 5.0 objectives. Next, we emphasizes the incorporation of ML techniques to improve manufacturing productivity and optimize decision-making processes. Even with advancements, Industry 5.0 may suffer several challenges and limitations, such as intelligent decision-making, security, data privacy, etc. To address the challenges of Industry 5.0, it is crucial to comprehend its protocols, which this survey examines alongside relevant technologies. Therefore, our survey also explores the primary challenges encountered when incorporating ML into Industry 5.0, such as integrating data, ensuring interoperability, and maintaining sustainability. Furthermore, the study elaborates on how these techniques drives substantial progress in various emerging applications by enhancing operational procedures and enabling innovative capabilities. Finally, we discuss potential research routes to overcome these hurdles and achieve the practical implementation of Industry 5.0.

Autores: Ruiz-Villafranca, Sergio and García-Sáez, Luis Miguel and Roldán-Gómez, José and Carrillo-Mondéjar, Javier and Gómez, Juan Manuel Castelo and Martínez, Jose Luis

Abstract: The rapid adoption of Industry 4.0/5.0 and Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has introduced new cybersecurity vulnerabilities in industrial operations. Título: Digital Twins as Enablers of Sustainable and Resilient Industry 5.0 Infrastructure: A Review
